title.en: Roll the World Wiki: Stars, Upgrades

description.en: Roll the World wiki for your first stars, smart upgrades and rare finds. Learn the beginner route, size milestones and how to unlock space in Roblox.

intro.en: Roll up objects smaller than your ball and grow from grass to city streets. Spend stardust on upgrades, equip rare finds and make stars to restart stronger. Reach your sixth star at size 300 to unlock space.

body.en: Roll over objects smaller than your ball, spend stardust on permanent upgrades, and make stars to restart with faster growth. The official route to space requires your sixth star at size 300.

description.en: A practical first-run route through grass, paths and streets, with controls, index claims and the first star explained.

intro.en: A practical first-run route through grass, paths and streets, with controls, index claims and the first star explained.

body.en: Use WASD to roll, right-drag to look and hold Shift to boost on PC. Collect smaller objects, check the size ring and use permanent growth upgrades before your first star.

paragraphs.en: The opening PC tutorial shows WASD to roll, right-drag to look, and hold Shift to boost. The size ring sits at the bottom left, with stars and purple stardust beside it. The right column contains shop, index, finds, boards, upgrades and settings.
These keys are verified from the PC recording. Use your platform’s on-screen controls on mobile or console. The official listing supports both, but exact controller mappings have not been verified.

title.en: Move from small objects to crowded streets

paragraphs.en: Start with the small pieces around the grass. Keep moving through objects that attach to your ball. If a target does not stick, collect smaller nearby objects and come back after the size ring grows.

The reviewed run moves through paths and park areas before town streets. This frame shows a ball at 8.47 studs beside planted rows and a road. It is one recorded route, with upgrades affecting the pace. It is not a mandatory area unlock threshold.
Open upgrades using the green arrow. The panel says stars keep upgrades and stardust, so an early growth level helps later runs too. Compare the next cost with the effect before buying.
Watch the index button for a claim prompt after collecting new object types. Claiming it adds stardust to reinvest. In the footage, the claim button is separate from simply collecting an object.

The first-star threshold is 50 studs in the reviewed game. The first-star summary shows a ×1.25 growth multiplier and the next star at 100 studs. A star starts a fresh small-ball run. Read the star guide before resetting.
If progress slows, check that useful finds are equipped, collect pending index rewards and return to clusters of smaller objects. No guaranteed completion time has been established.

description.en: What star resets keep, verified size milestones, growth multipliers and the route to the sixth star.

intro.en: What star resets keep, verified size milestones, growth multipliers and the route to the sixth star.

body.en: Stars reset your ball’s size and improve future growth. The first summary shows ×1.25 growth and a second-star target of 100 studs. Space requires star six at size 300.

title.en: What changes when you make a star

paragraphs.en: A star turns the run into a star-life summary, then starts a new run. The upgrades panel confirms that upgrades and stardust are retained. The Finds panel still contains the collection immediately after the first reset.
The first summary records 51.4 studs at the end of that run and the next-star target at 100. Finishing above the threshold is possible; 51.4 is not the required first-star size.
Directly checked milestones are listed below. An unverified row is left open instead of extending a numeric pattern.

title.en: Read the next requirement after a reset

paragraphs.en: Open upgrades and scroll to the star row. After star four, the reviewed panel says star 5 at 250, shows growth ×1.40 to ×1.45, and offers one star spin. These are recorded-build values. Check your live panel.
If the button says NOT BIG ENOUGH, keep collecting until the size target in that row is met. A large ball on an earlier star does not satisfy the sixth-star space requirement.

For progression, making a star when eligible gives the next run the higher growth multiplier. For exploration, you can continue after the prompt appears; the video shows a ball far above its current reset target.
Choose based on whether you want later stars or more exploration in this run. No mathematically optimal reset schedule has been verified.

description.en: Compare growth, speed, stamina, magnet, luck and start size using the real upgrade panel.

intro.en: Compare growth, speed, stamina, magnet, luck and start size using the real upgrade panel.

body.en: Spend stardust in upgrades. Growth improves collection progress, speed changes rolling speed, stamina improves boost and magnet extends reach. Stars keep upgrades and stardust.

paragraphs.en: Open the green upgrades arrow. The purple number is your stardust balance. Each row shows current level, current effect, next effect and price. Compare those before buying.
In the early recording, growth level 1 shows +5% to +10% growth while speed, stamina and magnet remain at level 0. The success message confirms that the purchased level makes growth 5% faster.

title.en: Which upgrade solves your current problem?

paragraphs.en: This editorial decision aid follows visible effects. It is not a measured ranking of stardust efficiency.

rows.en: You are focusing on rare finds

paragraphs.en: Check growth first because it directly supports reaching larger targets. Then choose movement upgrades or luck according to the delay you are experiencing. Targeted purchases are easier to assess than dividing every balance across all rows.
The later panel shows independent levels for growth, speed, stamina, magnet and luck. Costs change by level, so screenshots should not become a fixed shopping list.
The index claim prompt pays stardust after new collections. Finds also have a sell action with a displayed stardust value. Review useful bonuses and lock valuable items before selling.
If a purchase is unavailable, compare your balance with its current price. Stars keep the balance and upgrades, so you do not need to spend everything solely because a reset is available.

description.en: Equip bonuses, protect useful rolls with locks, compare effects and sell unwanted finds carefully.

intro.en: Equip bonuses, protect useful rolls with locks, compare effects and sell unwanted finds carefully.

body.en: Open finds, compare each effect and equip useful bonuses. Use LOCK before bulk selling. The menu says locked and equipped finds are kept during bulk sales.

paragraphs.en: The menu shows equipped slots and combined growth and stardust multipliers. This frame reads equipped 3/4. Each row has a name, bonus, odds label and LOCK, SELL, EQUIP or UNEQUIP controls.

Diamond Brick Shops shows +15.1% growth with an EQUIP button; Golden Hedge shows +5.5% growth and is already equipped. These are recorded examples. Compare actual effects instead of assuming every find in a rarity shares one bonus.

title.en: Why a rare object can disappear

paragraphs.en: The second reviewed video shows a tutorial explaining that rares are shared: the first player to roll one up keeps it. A rare object in the world is contested until collected.
If another player arrives first, find other eligible objects and keep growing. A shared spawn differs from an item already saved in Finds. A world announcement does not guarantee a personal reward.
ALL GOLDEN and ALL DIAMOND are bulk actions. The menu explicitly says locked and equipped finds are kept. Lock any item you intend to save, including when temporarily changing equipped items.
For a single unwanted item, read its SELL value. Before bulk selling, inspect protection states. Selling trades the find for displayed stardust; no undo mechanism has been verified.

title.en: Known rarity names and unknown odds

paragraphs.en: The developer names golden, diamond, rainbow and rarer variants, plus haunted finds for Halloween. The footage confirms item-specific bonuses and odds labels.

A 1 in 300 label belongs to the displayed find and its recorded context. The full loot table, luck stacking formula and universal odds per rarity are unverified. No complete drop-rate table is published here.

description.en: Recognize park, city, Mushroom Hollow and Starfall Range landmarks without confusing observed size with an unlock requirement.

intro.en: Recognize park, city, Mushroom Hollow and Starfall Range landmarks without confusing observed size with an unlock requirement.

body.en: Use the size ring and nearby objects to choose your route. Named areas are visible in gameplay, but an observed entry size does not establish a minimum requirement.

paragraphs.en: Move from tiny grass objects through paths, park furniture and streets as your size grows. Town blocks put many object types close together when they are small enough to collect.
If a target stays in place, collect smaller objects and return. A complete verified table of per-object size requirements is unavailable.
The recording shows the Mushroom Hollow banner, mountains and large plants at about 218 studs. This is an orientation example in a developed run, not a confirmed 218-stud gate.
Keep eligible trees and smaller scenery on your route instead of repeatedly pushing into an oversized target. Check the size ring alongside the ball’s appearance.
The Starfall Range banner appears over a broad map view. Roads, water and city blocks remain useful landmarks as your ball travels longer distances.
The Make a Star prompt remains available here. A large map view and entering space have separate conditions: the official space route requires star six at size 300.

title.en: When scenery becomes hard to read

paragraphs.en: Inspect settings if the scene becomes difficult to navigate. Community guidance mentions performance mode, but the exact toggle and ideal graphics value were not independently checked.
Adjust for your device and confirm that ground, nearby objects and UI remain visible. No universal best graphics level is established.

title.en: How to Unlock Space in Roll the World

description.en: The confirmed free space requirement, how stars differ from size, and which later progression details remain unverified.

intro.en: The confirmed free space requirement, how stars differ from size, and which later progression details remain unverified.

body.en: Make your sixth star at size 300 to leave Earth. This requirement appears in the official Roblox description and the reviewed upgrades banner.

paragraphs.en: Build your star count through repeated runs. Before a reset, open upgrades and read the next requirement. Collect until its button is available, then make the star.
A size-300 ball on an earlier star is insufficient evidence of eligibility. Track both the completed star count and size ring.

title.en: If you are still on Earth

paragraphs.en: Check your completed stars, read the next-star row and inspect the space button in the right-hand HUD. Follow the updated in-game requirement if it differs from older footage.
The reviewed full run ends at star four. It confirms the requirement banner but does not show the Earth-to-space transition. Exact transition clicks and a post-unlock screenshot remain unverified.
The official description says space lets you roll up planets, the sun, stars and the whole universe. It does not provide a full target order, size table or completion rewards.
Planet order, the full space map, Big Bang reset formulas and rewards are not independently verified. Earth values are not extended into a speculative space table.
The upgrades panel advertises a space pack as an alternative. The free sixth-star route is explicitly available. No purchase is needed to follow this guide.
Read current pack prices and contents in the game before spending. Old recorded prices can change; this guide does not recommend buying a skip.

intro.en: The officially listed 1000LIKES reward, shop redemption guidance and checks for failed codes.

body.en: The official description lists 1000LIKES for 5 star spins, 3 growth potions and 2× luck for 30 minutes. Checked October 26, 2026; not redeemed on our own account.

paragraphs.en: This table records the developer’s advertised reward. It does not promise a repeat redemption on an account that has already claimed it.

rows.en: 5 star spins; 3 growth potions; 2× luck for 30 minutes
Officially listed October 26; not personally redeemed

paragraphs.en: Open shop from the right HUD. English code guides describe a codes tab in the shop’s lower-left. Enter 1000LIKES and use the redemption action.

The shop button is visible in gameplay, but the selected videos never show the code field. Tab location comes from secondary guidance and should be matched to the current UI. No invented redemption-screen image is used.
Check spelling, remove spaces and read the exact in-game response. The code may have expired or already been used. Exact error messages and account reuse rules have not been independently checked.
The official listing promises a new code at 2,000 likes. This does not establish the code text or prove release. No guessed milestone code is included.
The official description offers +10% growth and the overzeer eye skin for joining the overzeer group. Follow the creator link from the official experience to verify the group.
Older 250LIKES and 500LIKES strings appear in community history. Current status and exact rewards were not verified, so they are excluded from this list.

description.en: Confirmed seasonal systems and Halloween features, with unknown schedules and rewards kept separate.

intro.en: Confirmed seasonal systems and Halloween features, with unknown schedules and rewards kept separate.

body.en: The developer confirms day and night, seasons, meteor showers and eruptions. Halloween is advertised through November 9 with zombie nights, pumpkins and haunted finds.

paragraphs.en: The reviewed run shows the town under different seasonal and lighting conditions. This frame shows a nighttime winter scene with clock and season information at the top.
Snow does not necessarily indicate a separate map. Continue judging collection by your size and nearby objects.
The current developer description lists zombie nights, pumpkins and haunted finds, with November 9 as the advertised end date. An exact end hour and time zone are not supplied.
The selected frames do not establish zombie damage, pumpkin rewards, haunted odds or post-event retention. Read live event messages and lock items you want to keep.
Both types are named by the developer. Watch nearby scenery and announcements while following your collection route. Exact event schedules and rewards are unverified.
Do not treat another player’s announcement as a guaranteed personal drop. Shared rare objects belong to the first player who collects them.
Community pages describe paid events and multipliers. The reviewed material does not verify every current cost and effect, so no paid-event price list is published.
For steady progress, collect eligible objects, claim index rewards and use permanent upgrades while waiting for a visible event.

body.en: This fan guide covers Roll the World by overzeer on Roblox: Place 97342490021056 and Universe 10769594564.

paragraphs.en: The official API identifies developer group overzeer, ID 5357472. The canonical experience uses Place 97342490021056 and Universe 10769594564.
Search results for the separate Steam title are excluded.
The developer description was compared with English guide pages and extracted gameplay frames. Screenshots illustrate observed UI; they do not represent site-owned play sessions.
Recordings were published October 24 and 25, 2026. Raw frame times, URLs and passage bindings remain in the project evidence. Current servers can differ after updates.
The actual space transition, full planet order, third-star threshold, full find probability table, live code redemption and post-Halloween retention remain unverified.
Developer claims, visible gameplay and editorial advice are distinguished. Advertised rewards are recorded without claiming personal redemption.

This independent guide uses Google Analytics 4 to understand page visits and usage. Google may use cookies and collect technical information such as device type, approximate location and page interactions. Browser privacy controls and content blockers can limit analytics collection.

We do not offer accounts or ask players to submit personal information on this site. External Roblox and YouTube links open services with their own privacy policies. Advertising is disabled on this release.

This guide provides general gameplay information and is not affiliated with Roblox or overzeer. Game updates can change mechanics, rewards and code availability. Check the current in-game prompt before spending currency or resetting progress.

Game names, artwork and screenshots belong to their respective owners. Community gameplay is identified separately from developer information. We do not guarantee game outcomes or the continued availability of third-party services.
